description: Radon is a chemical element with symbol Rn and atomic number 86. It is a radioactive noble gas that is colorless, odorless, and tasteless. Of the three naturally occurring radon isotopes, only 222Rn has a sufficiently long half-life of 3.825 days to be released from soil and rock where it is generated.
uses: Radon can be used as a natural tracer in physical sciences due to its 3.8-day half-life. Techniques such as sub-slab depressurization are used for radon mitigation in buildings. Radon compounds have been considered for radon gas removal in uranium mines.
characteristics: Radon is the densest of the noble gases with a density of 9.73 kg/m³ at standard temperature and pressure, about 8 times denser than Earth's atmosphere. It forms a monatomic gas and is colorless at standard conditions; when cooled below its boiling point of 211.5 K, concentrated liquid radon emits radioluminescence of varying color. Radon is chemically inert to most common reactions due to its eight electrons in the outer valence shell, though it is more reactive than xenon and can form compounds with powerful oxidizing agents such as fluorine.
